oil.summary: WTI and Brent posted modest daily gains — +1.71% to $83.64 and +0.89% to $88.62 respectively — even as the broader weekly tape remains deeply in the red (-4.77% and -5.50%). The divergence reflects competing forces: Hormuz risk premium has not fully collapsed, with China today publicly demanding the strait reopen and slamming new US Iran sanctions, while Secretary Rubio signalled no further strikes on Iran for now. On the supply side, Ukraine's confirmed drone strike on Russia's Afipsky refinery in Krasnodar adds a downstream disruption narrative, forcing Moscow to turn to India for refined product. A temporary US easing of Russia oil sanctions — reported Wednesday and already riling European allies — partially capped the upside. The dramatic RBOB plunge of -9.94% in a single session stands out and likely reflects refinery-supply re-pricing post-strike rather than demand destruction. EUA OPEC options still price a 77% probability of a cut at the next meeting.
drivers: Hormuz/Iran sanctions uncertainty: US tightening Iran oil sanctions while signalling a pause in strikes kept a geopolitical floor under crude, though markets slipped on easing fears earlier in the week
Ukraine drone strike on Afipsky refinery in Krasnodar disrupted Russian refining capacity, sending Russia to India for petrol supply and contributing to RBOB's sharp -9.94% single-day drop
US temporary easing of Russia oil sanctions to tame price surge — opposed by European allies — and TotalEnergies' full exit from Arctic LNG 2 reshaped the Russian supply outlook

gas.summary: Natural gas prices rallied sharply on both sides of the Atlantic. Henry Hub climbed +2.15% to $2.903/MMBtu, extending a solid +6.22% weekly gain, while TTF surged +4.84% to €68.80/MWh — up nearly 14% on the month. The dominant driver is a structural European storage deficit: the continent is entering winter with gas inventories at a two-decade low, a situation exacerbated by Middle East conflict disrupting LNG supply chains. TotalEnergies' completed exit from Russia's Arctic LNG 2 project removes another marginal supply source from the market. On the M&A side, Energean entering exclusive talks for a ~$1 billion acquisition of BP's Egyptian gas assets signals that buyers are urgently seeking to secure non-Russian, non-Hormuz-exposed supply. The setup into winter looks acutely tight for European buyers.
drivers: European gas storage at a two-decade seasonal low heading into winter, with Middle East conflict having curtailed LNG supply — primary bullish catalyst for TTF's +13.87% monthly gain
TotalEnergies completes exit from Russia's Arctic LNG 2, transferring its 10% stake to Novatek and further constraining sanctioned Russian LNG supply to Europe
Energean in exclusive talks for ~$1 billion BP Egypt gas asset acquisition, reflecting urgent buy-side appetite for non-Russian, non-Hormuz gas supply

power.summary: The power and carbon complex presents a mixed picture. EU EUAs dipped marginally (-0.57% to $78.155/EUA) and are essentially flat on the week, though TTF's sharp rally will mechanically lift gas-fired generation costs and could provide EUA support if coal-to-gas switching increases. On the structural demand side, a report today highlighted the AI boom as a primary driver of accelerating US data-centre electricity demand. In India, 45 coal-fired plants are operating at critically low coal stock levels amid rising demand — an El Niño-related stress signal. Fortum filed a state aid application in Sweden for a major new nuclear project, while the Trump administration continued its dual-track energy policy: attacking offshore wind (leaving workers in limbo) while the DoE begins tests for fracked geothermal as an alternative. The Saudi nuclear deal was formally sent to Congress.
drivers: TTF's +4.84% daily surge raises gas-fired generation costs across Europe, providing a potential floor for EUA prices if demand for carbon allowances from gas generators holds
AI-driven data-centre load growth identified as the dominant new US power demand vector, while India faces acute coal supply stress with 45 plants at critically low stock levels

Trump administration's energy policy divergence sharpens: offshore wind faces continued executive headwinds, while DoE advances fracked geothermal testing and Fortum pursues new nuclear capacity in Sweden
